dmm-2008-tiebreaker-01.title: Right triangles around a small square
dmm-2008-tiebreaker-01.body:
By the congruence $\triangle ABH\cong\triangle BCI$ (with $A\to B$, $B\to C$, $H\to I$) we have $\angle HAB=\angle IBC$. Since $I$ lies on ray $BH$, $\angle ABH+\angle IBC=\angle ABC=90^\circ$. Hence $\angle HAB+\angle ABH=90^\circ$ and $\angle AHB=90^\circ$.

Let $AH=p$ and $BH=q$, so $AB=s=\sqrt{p^2+q^2}$. By congruence ($A\to B$, $B\to C$, $H\to I$), $BI=AH=p$. Since $H$ lies on $BI$, $HI=p-q$; by the four-fold symmetry $GHIJ$ is a square of side $GH=p-q$.

Inradius of a right triangle: $r=\dfrac{p+q-s}2$. The inradius of the small square is $\dfrac{p-q}2$. Equal radii give $p+q-s=p-q$, so $s=2q$ and $p=\sqrt{s^2-q^2}=\sqrt3\,q$.

Therefore $\dfrac{AB}{GH}=\dfrac{2q}{(\sqrt3-1)q}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3-1}=\sqrt3+1$.

**Answer: $1+\sqrt3$**

dmm-2008-tiebreaker-02.title: Dirichlet kernel
dmm-2008-tiebreaker-02.body:
Put $x=2\cos\theta$. Then $x^3-3x=2\cos3\theta$ and $x^2-2=2\cos2\theta$, so
$$x^3+x^2-2x-1=(x^3-3x)+(x^2-2)+x+1=1+2\cos\theta+2\cos2\theta+2\cos3\theta=\frac{\sin(7\theta/2)}{\sin(\theta/2)}.$$
(The last equality is the standard identity $1+2\sum_{j=1}^{3}\cos j\theta=\frac{\sin(7\theta/2)}{\sin(\theta/2)}$.) This vanishes for $\theta=\frac{2\pi m}7$, $m=1,2,3$ (and $\sin(\theta/2)\ne0$), giving three distinct roots $2\cos\frac{2\pi}7,2\cos\frac{4\pi}7,2\cos\frac{6\pi}7$ of the cubic: all of them. With $\theta=k\pi$ and $0\le k\le1$ in increasing order, $k=\frac27,\frac47,\frac67$.

**Answer: $\left(\frac27,\frac47,\frac67\right)$**

dmm-2008-tiebreaker-03.title: Euler's formula
dmm-2008-tiebreaker-03.body:
Let $D$ be the number of decagons, $V,E,F$ vertices, edges, faces. Each vertex has degree $3$, so $2E=3V$. Counting edge-face incidences, $2E=3\cdot20+10D$. Also $F=20+D$. Then $V=\frac{2E}{3}$, so
$$V-E+F=\frac{2E}3-E+20+D=2\;\Rightarrow\;-\frac{E}{3}+D=-18.$$
With $E=30+5D$: $-10-\frac{5D}3+D=-18$, so $\frac{2D}3=8$ and $D=12$.

**Answer: 12**

dmm-2008-tiebreaker-04.title: Subtract the equations
dmm-2008-tiebreaker-04.body:
$P_1$: $x=a(y-1)^2$ through $(2,2)$ gives $a=2$: $x=2(y-1)^2$. $P_2$: $y=b(x-1)^2$ through $(2,2)$ gives $b=2$: $y=2(x-1)^2$.

Subtracting, $x-y=2\big[(y-1)^2-(x-1)^2\big]=2(y-x)(x+y-2)$, so $(x-y)\big(1+2(x+y-2)\big)=0$.

*Case $x=y$:* $x=2(x-1)^2\Rightarrow2x^2-5x+2=0\Rightarrow x=2$ or $\frac12$: points $(2,2)$, $\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)$.

*Case $x+y=\frac32$:* $y=\frac32-x$, so $x=2\left(\frac12-x\right)^2$, i.e. $4x^2-6x+1=0$, $x=\frac{3\pm\sqrt5}4$, $y=\frac{3\mp\sqrt5}4$.

**Answer:** $(2,2)$, $\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)$, $\left(\frac{3-\sqrt5}4,\frac{3+\sqrt5}4\right)$, $\left(\frac{3+\sqrt5}4,\frac{3-\sqrt5}4\right)$.
